'''Xavier Tolsa''' (born 1966) is a [[Spaniards|Spanish]] mathematician, specializing in analysis.

Tolsa is a professor at the [[Autonomous University of Barcelona]] and at the [[Catalan Institution for Research and Advanced Studies|''Institució Catalana de Recerca i Estudis Avançats'' (ICREA), the Catalan Institute for Advanced Scientific Studies]].

Tolsa does research on [[harmonic analysis]] (Calderón-Zygmund theory), [[complex analysis]], [[geometric measure theory]], and [[potential theory]]. Specifically, he is known for his research on [[analytic capacity]] and [[Analytic capacity#Removable sets and Painlevé's problem|removable set]]s. He solved the problem of [[Anatoli Georgievich Vitushkin|A. G. Vitushkin]]<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1070/RM1967v022n06ABEH003763|title=The analytic capacity of sets in problems of approximation theory|journal=Russian Mathematical Surveys|volume=22|issue=6|pages=139–200|year=1967|last1=Vitushkin|first1=A. G.|bibcode=1967RuMaS..22..139V|s2cid=250869451 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=89A3gdCfPFUC|title = Vitushkin's Conjecture for Removable Sets|isbn = 9781441967091|last1 = Dudziak|first1 = James|date = 2011-02-03| publisher=Springer }}</ref> about the semi-additivity of analytic capacity. This enabled him to solve an even older problem of [[Paul Painlevé]] on the geometric characterization of removable sets. Tolsa succeeded in solving the Painlevé problem by using the concept of so-called curvatures of measures introduced by [[Mark Melnikov]] in 1995. Tolsa's proof involves estimates of Cauchy transforms. He has also done research on the so-called [[Guy David (mathematician)|David]]-[[Stephen Semmes|Semmes]] problem involving [[Riesz transform]]s and rectifiability.<ref>{{cite web|title=Xavier Tolsa, ICREA Research Professor|website=Departament de Matemàtiques Universitat Autonoma de Barcelona|url=http://mat.uab.es/~xtolsa/xtolsa.html}}</ref>

In 2002 he was awarded the [[Salem Prize]].<ref>[http://blocs.iec.cat/scm/files/2011/02/N17.pdf "Premi Salem"], ''Societat Catalana de Matemàtiques Notícies'', July 2002, n°17, page 9</ref> In 2006 in Madrid he was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] with talk ''Analytic capacity, rectifiability, and the Cauchy integral''. He received in 2004 the [[EMS Prize]]<ref>{{cite journal|title=Prizes Presented at the European Congress of Mathematicians|journal=Notices of the AMS|date=October 2004|volume=51|issue=9|pages=1070–1071|url=http://www.ams.org/notices/200409/people.pdf|archive-date=2017-09-21|access-date=2019-08-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170921175825/http://www.ams.org/notices/200409/people.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> and was an Invited Lecturer at the 2004 [[European Congress of Mathematics|ECM]] with talk ''Painlevé's problem, analytic capacity and curvature of measures''. In 2013 he received the [[Ferran Sunyer i Balaguer Prize]] for his monograph ''Analytic capacity, the Cauchy transform, and non-homogeneous Calderón-Zygmund theory'' (Birkhäuser Verlag, 2013}.<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=guW5BAAAQBAJ|title = Analytic Capacity, the Cauchy Transform, and Non-homogeneous Calderón–Zygmund Theory|isbn = 9783319005966|last1 = Tolsa|first1 = Xavier|date = 2013-12-16| publisher=Springer }}</ref> In 2019 he received the [[Premis Rei Jaume I|Rei Jaume I]] prize for his contributions to Mathematics.
